A `setSimulatedLatency(ms)` knob on `window.__monecraft.net` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS`) injects artificial delay for local testing. World owners can **revoke every outstanding invite link** in one click from the menu. The game server gains admin ops behind `ADMIN_TOKEN`: a per-room replay log (`GET /rooms/:id/log`) that `scripts/replay.ts` reconstructs offline, an owner **kick** (`POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`), and `/rooms` bandwidth (`kbOutPerSec`) alongside the tick gauges — plus `scripts/loadSim.ts`, a synthetic N-client soak that reports server tick p95 vs the 50 ms budget for tuning `MAX_ROOMS`. Net constants are documented in tuning.md and an ops runbook in online.md.

In-world you see the other players (named avatars overhead), share every block edit / mob / chest / day-night with them, and **chat** with `T`/`Enter`; a ping badge and disconnect notice track the connection. The client mounts the **same** renderer/audio/HUD/input stack on a _replica_ engine (`NetworkSession`, `lib/net/`): it worldgens byte-identically from the server's seed, applies the gzipped world sync, predicts only its own movement (streamed at tick rate; the server clamps speed/teleports and owns hunger/health/inventory via change-only self-deltas), renders remote players and mobs ~125 ms in the past from interpolation buffers, and reroutes gameplay commands up the wire through the engine's `routeDispatch` hook — so the input controller and every UI panel behave exactly as in single-player. Pause is personal (the world keeps running; "Save & Quit" becomes "Leave world"), the night skips only when everyone's in bed, and mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT). A full-stack Playwright spec (`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`) drives two browsers through invite → join → shared edit → chat against the real Next app (on an in-process `pglite://memory` Postgres) and Bun game server, no external services. **v1 scope cuts**: rafts/ships aren't boardable online, in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only their hits), and advancements/stats accrue to the room's primary player only.

The engine gains authority-aware remote-pose application and can construct playerless rooms (bootPlayer: false).
- **Online accounts, cloud saves & invites (groundwork)**: better-auth identities with instant anonymous guests — upgrading to a real account (sign-up or sign-in while playing as guest) re-parents the guest's worlds/memberships/invites onto the new account, proven by an integration test against real better-auth + real SQL (PGlite). Drizzle/Postgres schema for worlds, memberships, and invite links; membership-gated world CRUD; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses; gzipped single-player cloud-save blobs with last-write-wins conflict detection; and 60-second HS256 join tickets — the only trust link the future game server needs (it never sees cookies). Menu gains an Account panel. Fully offline-first: until the player takes an online action, the client makes no auth requests at all.

### Changed

- **Multi-player engine core** (save **v16→v17**; single-player behavior unchanged — the full e2e suite passes as before): the engine now models N players in one world, with single-player as the one-entry case of the same state. `GameState.players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>` absorbs every per-player field (inventory, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player timers); the old flat fields remain as accessor aliases onto the primary player for the shell/tests/console, with an ESLint guard banning them inside engine systems. All 23 systems take the acting player explicitly: mobs hunt the nearest targetable player (Creative/Spectator excluded) and anchor flee/pet-follow on the nearest of any mode; arrows/explosions hit any/all players in range; spawn directors center waves on a random party member and scale the hostile cap by `ceil(players/2)`; dungeon spawners arm for any player in radius; random ticks split their budget across players; raid rewards pay every living player. The night skips only when **every** eligible player is in bed (new `wakeUp` command backs out pre-fade). `dispatch`/`applyLook` take the commanding player's id; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (join restores the persisted v17 slice, leave serializes it back), `setPlayerInput`, and the `authority`/`headless` engine options are the surface a multiplayer server drives. Key bindings and cursor capture now live entirely in `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`; the engine simulates the same regardless of input source, which is what a multiplayer client's per-tick intent packets (and a future keybinding screen) require.
- **Tick driver extraction** (no behavior change): the rAF loop's catch-up substepping moved from `useMinecraftGame` into `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts` (`createAccumulator`), alongside a new drift-corrected `createFixedTicker` — the 20 Hz driver a headless multiplayer server will step worlds with. Unit-tested with a fake clock (catch-up, debt-drop cap, no drift under chronically-late callbacks).
- **Portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` **10→11**, save schema stays v16): all seed-determined noise — terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, underground speckle/flora hashes, weather windows, the daylight curve — moved from engine-defined `Math.sin` to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`), so the same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**. This is the groundwork for online multiplayer (a Bun server and browser clients must agree on the generated baseline to sync worlds as seed + block diff) and retires the fragile "worldgen hashes are only valid on the pinned Bun" caveat. Terrain is visually unchanged (same formulas; every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched), but exact bytes shift: **existing worlds reboot from their seed and discard block edits**, per the standard worldgen-bump policy. Digests re-baselined into the new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`; a new Playwright spec (`e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`) proves Chromium/V8 regenerates the exact Bun/JSC baseline.

  - **Villages**: clusters of houses generate on flat, dry land — terraced and built so they're actually visible (the old loose houses rarely fit natural terrain, so they barely appeared). Villager **residents** spawn and live there and **persist with the world**; villagers no longer scatter loosely (a village-less seed falls back to a few wandering ones near spawn, so trading is always available). Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** — existing worlds of the old version reboot from their seed, and the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined — with no save-schema change for the villages themselves (residents ride the v14 `mobs` field). Villages run on their own decoupled PRNG (`villageRand`) placed last, so every other generation pass stays byte-identical to a village-less world of the same seed.
  - **Villager professions**: each villager is a **farmer, blacksmith, librarian, or cleric** and offers only its own slice of the trade economy (a sell + a buy each), its smock tinted to its profession. Opening a villager filters the Trading recipe book to its offers and gates the craft command — you can't craft a blacksmith trade while talking to a farmer (a spoof guard on dispatch, not just the UI). Save schema bumps **v14→v15** (a resident's additive `profession` on its `SavedMob`; pre-v15 villagers load professionless and the engine assigns one).
  - **Raids**: a craftable **Ominous Horn** (3 gold ore + 2 bone + 4 gunpowder) sounded near a village calls down **`RAID_WAVE_COUNT` (3)** waves of a new **raider** mob; clear them all for an emerald + XP reward, or — if every nearby villager dies first — the village falls. Raiders hunt villagers (and your pets defend), reusing the mob allegiance and mob-vs-mob combat from PR 1, so they needed no AI change. A raid is transient (`state.raid`, like the boss — a reload cancels it), so there's no save bump beyond the additive horn item; worldgen is unchanged (stays 9).
- **Tameable companions & a living mob world** (Living World, PR 1 of 2): wolves and cats now roam the world, and feeding a wild one its treat — a **bone** for a wolf, **raw fish** for a cat — tames it (a ~1-in-3 `TAME_CHANCE`; the treat is eaten either way). A tamed pet becomes a loyal **ally** that follows you, **sits/stays** on a right-click (holding a non-treat), and **fights hostiles for you** — its kills drop loot and XP straight to you. It recalls (teleports) to you past `PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE`, and **survives save/reload** — the first mob the game ever persists. Bred pets pass on their ownership, so puppies and kittens are owned allies too. Zero new assets (procedural wolf/cat models + ZZFX barks/meows); the save schema bumps **v13 → v14** (additive persisted pets), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
  - This lands two reusable foundations. **Mob allegiance**: every mob carries a `faction` (wild/hostile/ally/villager/raider) that drives a shared enmity table, so mobs fight _each other_ — hostiles now hunt and attack **villagers** (who flee), and your pets defend you. A fighter re-scans for the nearest enemy only every `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS`, so the per-frame mob tick stays O(N); mob-vs-mob combat is melee-only and uses raw damage (difficulty scales player-facing hits only). A kill credits loot/XP by the **victim's** faction — a pet's kill feeds you, a slain villager or pet yields nothing. **Mob persistence**: a minimal `SavedMob` (only tamed pets in this release) round-trips through `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs`, re-grounding each pet onto the current surface on load; the fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot as before
- **Advancements & statistics**: the game gains a progression meta — running **statistics** (blocks mined, monsters slain, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, animals bred, distance travelled, time played, deaths, jumps, villager trades) and a tight, flat set of **16 advancements**, one per major system (mine a log/stone/sliver/diamond, craft a pickaxe, craft a furnace, fire a bow, slay a hostile, defeat the Dragon Lord, breed animals, harvest wheat, catch a fish, enchant an item, drink a potion, sleep, trade with a villager). All on **zero new assets** — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — and the save schema bumps **v12 → v13** (additive), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
  - Press **L** to open a dedicated two-tab overlay (mutually exclusive with the inventory; the pause menu won't open over it): an **Advancements** grid grouped by category with locked/unlocked styling, and a **Statistics** list of the counters. Each unlock raises an _"Advancement Unlocked"_ toast and a celebratory chime
  - **Persist across death.** Like `xp` and unlike status `effects`, both stats and advancements are a long-term record that survives a death (`clearEffects` never touches them) and a reload
  - **Architecture**: one observer at the engine's single `emit` chokepoint folds every gameplay event into the stat counters (`recordEvent`), then unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed and announces it (`advancementUnlocked` event) — no per-system bookkeeping. The whole set is a **declarative registry** in `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts` (`{ stat, threshold }` per row), so `evaluateAdvancements` is pure and adding one is a one-line edit. A new broadly-useful `crafted` event drives the craft/brew/trade counters; `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`) is the single source of truth for counting hostile kills. The overlay reads detail through a new `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render, so play never churns the snapshot with stat values the HUD doesn't show

## [0.11.0] - 2026-06-28

### Fixed

- **Equipped armor no longer occupies a hotbar/inventory slot.** Armor was equipped _by reference_ — the worn piece stayed in the inventory and kept occupying its slot (and rendered twice: once in the hotbar/grid, once in the armor column). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (freeing the slot, ending the double-render), and unequipping returns it to a free inventory slot (refused when the inventory is full, so nothing is lost). `EquippedArmor` now holds the worn `InventorySlot` instances; the defense/durability/Mending seams read them directly (no more find-by-id, which also removes the duplicate-piece ambiguity). The save schema bumps **v11 → v12** — `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName) — with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)

Each is an engine-only buff with a procedurally-painted HUD icon (no renderer change); the three effect ids ride the existing top-level `effects` field (added to `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`), so no save bump
- **Tool & armor enchantments — Fortune & Feather Falling**: on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Fortune** (tools) rolls up to `FORTUNE_BONUS_PER_LEVEL` (1) extra of an **ore** per level when you mine it (gated to the ore blocks in `rollBlockDrops`, read off the mining tool). **Feather Falling** (boots only, via the `itemIds` allow-list) cuts fall damage by `FEATHER_FALLING_REDUCE_PER_LEVEL` (0.15) per level — capped at `FEATHER_FALLING_MAX_REDUCTION` (0.8) — read off the worn boots at the `tickPlayerMotion` fall seam. Both ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump
- **Weapon enchantments — Knockback & Looting**: two new enchantments for any weapon, on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Knockback** adds `KNOCKBACK_PER_LEVEL` (0.4) to the melee shove per level (the base shove is now the named `MELEE_KNOCKBACK_IMPULSE` (0.75), no longer a magic number), read off the held weapon at the `tryAttackMob` seam. **Looting** rolls up to `LOOTING_BONUS_PER_LEVEL` (1) extra of each mob drop per level on a **melee** kill (the killing weapon's level is forwarded through the kill callback, so arrows/thrown spears/explosions apply none), in `rollMobDrops`. Both ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump
- **Bow enchantments — Power & Punch**: two new enchantments for the existing enchanting table, on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Power** adds `POWER_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL` (2) arrow damage per level and **Punch** adds `PUNCH_KNOCKBACK_PER_LEVEL` (0.25) arrow knockback per level, both read off the held bow at the single `tryFireBow` seam. They're **bow-only**: `EnchantmentDef` gains an optional `itemIds` allow-list (`canEnchant` honors it on top of the item-kind gate), so these don't appear on swords (which are also `weapon`). Their ids ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
- **Equipped armor now shows on the player** in third-person (press **V**). Each worn piece renders as a procedurally-built voxel "shell" over the matching body part (helmet → head, face mask → visor, neck protection → collar, chestplate → torso + shoulder caps, leggings → upper legs, boots → feet), parented to the limb pivots so it animates with the walk/attack gait, and tinted toward the ore it's crafted from. Renderer-only (`playerModel.ts` builds the shells, `playerVisuals.ts` toggles each by what's worn) — zero new assets, no engine/save change
- **Grindstone**: a new crafted station (**2 cobble + 2 planks**) — the anvil's inverse, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted stone-wheel block, reusing existing synth) and **no save-format or worldgen change**. Right-click to open the grindstone panel; with **enchanted** gear selected in the hotbar, **Remove enchantments** strips them all and refunds **`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP per level** removed. Pure logic in `lib/game/grindstone.ts`, a new `grindstoneStrip` command, and a `GrindstoneColumn` panel; the `Grindstone` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 54), craft-only, so no worldgen baseline change

The save schema bumps **v10 → v11** (additive `customName`), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
  - Right-click to open the anvil panel, which — like the enchanting table — acts on the **selected hotbar** tool/weapon/armor and spends XP levels.   - **Architecture**: the new `Anvil` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 53) so saved block ids never shift, and it's craft-only so no worldgen baseline changes. Pure logic lives in `lib/game/anvil.ts` (`combineSlots`, `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`, `materialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`), driven by new `anvilCombine`/`anvilRepair`/`anvilRename` commands. # Codebase state report: six systems

## 1. Vehicle system (rafts/ships)

**Files:** `lib/game/engine/systems/vehicles.ts` (all logic), `lib/game/render/vehicleVisuals.ts` (render), `VehicleState` in `lib/game/engine/state.ts:199`, config in `lib/game/config.ts:14-24`.

**Representation:** A vehicle is a **free entity with a float position**, not a block. `VehicleState = { id, kind, position: THREE.Vector3, yaw, rider: PlayerId | null }` (state.ts:199-205). They live in `state.vehicles: VehicleState[]` + `state.nextVehicleId` (state.ts:361). `VehicleKind = "raft" | "ship"` (types.ts:122); per-kind tuning via a `VEHICLE_SPECS` record (vehicles.ts:36).

**Boarding/riding:** `mountVehicle` sets `vehicle.rider = player.id` and `player.mountedVehicleId = vehicle.id` (vehicles.ts:135) — a bidirectional link. Two board paths: aimed raycast board (`tryBoardAimedVehicle`, VEHICLE_BOARD_REACH=4.5, vehicles.ts:205) and auto-board when walking onto a ship's deck (`tickVehicles` fallback loop, vehicles.ts:259). `syncPlayerToVehicle` snaps the rider to the boat, zeroes velocity, sets onGround, and player physics is skipped while mounted (vehicles.ts:176).

**Movement while mounted:** `tickVehicles` (vehicles.ts:238) reads `input.move`: forward/back = **direct position integration** along the yaw-forward vector (`position += forward * speed * dt`), NOT a physics force; left/right = yaw turn (VEHICLE_TURN_RATE); crouch = dismount. Every move is gated by `canOccupy` → `vehicleHasWaterSupport` (4 corners + center must be Water below and Air at deck) + in-bounds + no vehicle overlap (vehicles.ts:97-133). A blocked move is reverted to the previous position.

**Persistence:** Save field `vehicles?: SavedVehicle[]` added in save v16 (types.ts:351-356). `SavedVehicle = { kind, x, y, z, yaw }` (types.ts:315) — no id, no rider (rider is session-only). `serializeVehicles`/`restoreVehicles` (save.ts:357-374); `restoreVehicle` rebuilds unconditionally with no re-validation (vehicles.ts:55). `MAX_VEHICLES=64` bounds save size.

**Multiplayer (`vp` channel):** `VehiclePose = { id, kind, x, y, z, yaw, riderId }` (protocol.ts:127). Server owns mounted motion; `riderId` is cosmetic on clients. Full set ships in the sync snapshot (`vehicles: VehiclePose[]`, protocol.ts:117); per-tick `vp?` deltas carry only vehicles that moved past a deadband (`collectVehiclePoses`, room.ts:588, uses `MOB_DEADBAND_SQ` + quantized pos/ang). Client applies via `upsertReplicaVehicle` (NetworkSession.ts:356). Replicas early-return before world systems.

**Minecart reuse verdict — mostly yes on the plumbing, no on movement:**
- **Reusable as-is (kind-agnostic):** the rider link (`mountedVehicleId` ↔ `rider`), persistence (`SavedVehicle` + save field + cap), and replication (`vp`/`VehiclePose` deadband). Adding `"minecart"` to the `VehicleKind` union + a `VEHICLE_SPECS` entry gets you riding, saving, and netcode nearly free.
- **Must be rewritten per-kind:** movement and placement are hardcoded to water. `tickVehicles` does free WASD steering; `canOccupy`/`vehicleHasWaterSupport` require a water column; `tryPlaceVehicle` is gated on `slot.id === "raft"|"ship"` and a `waterSurfaceRaycast` (vehicles.ts:212-236). A rail-guided cart needs a rail-follow movement function and a rail/ground support check — these three functions would need a per-kind branch/strategy.
- **Net-new:** there is no rail block. Rails would need new BlockIds + a mesher shape (flat — the redstone-overlay pattern already proves this, see §3).

## 2. Redstone system ("redstone-lite")

**Files:** `lib/world/redstone.ts` (pure id helpers), `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.ts` (simulation), BlockIds in `lib/world/blocks.ts:87-104`, tunables in `config.ts:210-217`.

**Block ids (58-69):** RedstoneWire 58/On 59, Lever 60/On 61, RedstoneButton 62/On 63, PressurePlate 64/On 65, RedstoneTorchOff 66/RedstoneTorch(lit) 67, RedstoneLamp 68/LampOn 69.

**Power representation = id parity** (rides the block diff, exactly like doors): even=off, odd=on. `redstoneOn(b)=b|1`, `redstoneOff(b)=b&~1`, `isRedstoneOn=(b&1)===1` (redstone.ts world helpers). A toggle is a single `blockChanges.set` write that gets relight + save-diff + net-journal for free. **Power itself is never persisted** — `RedstoneState` (cells set, button timers, prevDoorPowered, timer) is session-only (state.ts:391) and re-derived from the grid every pass. Boot recovers the component set by scanning the block diff (`seedRedstoneCells`, redstone.ts:49 — works because every component is craft-only/player-placed).

**Tick:** `tickRedstone` at fixed `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS=0.1` cadence (config.ts:213). Three phases (redstone.ts:123): (1) inputs & self-heal (pressure plates from occupied cells, button pop-back `REDSTONE_BUTTON_PRESS_SECONDS`, overlay-support checks), (2) power graph re-derived — sources power their 6 face neighbors, wire relaxes outward with a hop budget `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE=15` and ±1 slope climbing, (3) outputs written only on change (wire, lamp, torch-inverter). Runs server-side only; replicas receive the resulting block deltas.

**Powered-consumer seams (redstone.ts:267-299):** after computing the `powered` set, one loop dispatches on consumer block id: `Tnt` → `primeTnt` (idempotent), doors → `forceDoor` on rising/falling edge (tracked via `prevDoorPowered`). The lamp is even simpler — in Phase 3 it's just `powered.has(index)` → id swap (redstone.ts:251). **Adding a new powered consumer is low-friction:** for a level-triggered device add a branch to Phase 3 or the consumer loop; for an edge-triggered device add a `prev*` set like `prevDoorPowered`. A **powered rail is easy** (a consumer that flips a block-id variant / gates cart motion). Placement/interact seams already exist: `trackRedstoneCell` (redstone.ts:56), and right-click handled in `interact.ts:91-92` (`toggleLever`/`pressButton`).

**Moving/pushing blocks anywhere: NONE.** No piston, no block-translation, no "block in motion" state anywhere in the codebase. The only block "motion" is destruction (explosion/TNT) and in-place id swaps (doors, redstone). **A piston is net-new and much harder** than a powered rail — there is no block-entity that translates and no partial-tick block animation to build on.

## 3. Renderer/mesher block-shape assumptions

**File:** `lib/world/meshing.ts` (`buildGeometryBuffers`).

**Default = full unit cube** with per-face culling (hidden faces skipped), baked AO in vertex colors, atlas UVs, split into opaque + glass layers (meshing.ts:249-299).

**Partial geometry IS a first-class pattern.** Two special cases route to `pushBlockCuboid` — an **arbitrary inset box** (min/max on all three axes) rendered with no neighbor culling:
- **Redstone wire renders as a genuinely flat slab**, not a painted full cube: `redstoneBounds` for wire = a box `minY:0, maxY:0.07` inset 1/16 horizontally (world/redstone.ts:66). All redstone overlays (58-67) use this path (meshing.ts:263); the lamp (68-69) is a plain full cube.
- **Doors render as thin panels:** `doorBounds` = a 3/16-thick, full-height slab positioned per facing, rotating to the hinge edge when open (doors.ts:58-70; meshing.ts:255).

**Slabs/stairs/rails feasibility:** the inset-cuboid path already exists, so **slabs are trivial** (one half-height box) and **rails are trivial** (flat, exactly like wire). **Stairs** need two boxes — a small extension of the single-`pushBlockCuboid` pattern. Two caveats: (a) `pushBlockCuboid` draws all 6 faces uncconditionally (no culling), so a slab abutting a full block double-draws the shared face — a perf nit, not a blocker; (b) collision shape is separate — doors already carry a partial-AABB collision shape (`doorBounds`), so there's a template, but each new shape needs its own collision box (redstone overlays are deliberately non-colliding).

## 4. World/dimension model

**Single fixed volume.** `WORLD_SIZE_X=512, WORLD_SIZE_Y=150, WORLD_SIZE_Z=512` (blocks.ts:1-3). One `VoxelWorld` = a flat `Uint8Array(sizeX*sizeY*sizeZ)` block array + a parallel light array + a `seed` (voxelWorld.ts:15-33). `GameState.world` is a single instance; `state.mobs`, `state.containers`, `state.vehicles`, dungeon/village index sets are all keyed to that one world.

**Save = seed + block diff.** `SaveData` carries `seed: number` + `changes: Array<[number, number]>` — a sparse voxel-index→blockId diff over deterministically generated terrain (types.ts:146-147). Lighting is a derived cache (not saved); lava is worldgen (not saved). `WORLDGEN_VERSION=11` gates diff applicability (config.ts:390).

**Second dimension (Nether-like) is a substantial structural change.** It requires a **second VoxelWorld volume plus a second block-diff section** in the save, and dimension-keyed copies of mobs/containers/vehicles (all currently single-world in `GameState`). There is no existing "multiple co-existing worlds in one save" concept. (Note: there IS a multi-*world* feature in `lib/game/worlds.ts`, but those are separate save slots you load one at a time, not simultaneous dimensions.)

**Teleport/portal machinery: none for cross-space.** The only teleport-like code is `forceUnstuck` (GameEngine.ts:1598, nudges a wedged player to a safe cell) and pet recall (`PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE`, mobAI.ts:355). Spectator/Creative **noclip** (`isNoclip`, gameModes.ts:64) is free movement through blocks but stays in the same world. No portal block, no dimension transition, no "move player + swap world" seam — all net-new.

**Buckets: DO NOT EXIST.** No bucket item; no water/lava pickup or source placement anywhere (the only `bucket` matches are an unrelated recipe-bucketing helper in recipes.ts). Water (17) and Lava (47) are blocks, but Lava is worldgen-only and unmineable, and there's no item that scoops or places a fluid source. Fluid pickup/placement is net-new.

## 5. Status effects / potions and combat seams

**Effect definitions:** `EffectId` union (types.ts:12) = `speed | strength | regeneration | fire_resistance | water_breathing | haste | resistance | jump_boost | poison`. There is no literal `VALID_EFFECT_IDS` const — the union plus `EFFECT_ORDER` (statusEffects.ts:27) enumerate them. Effects live in `player.effects: Map<EffectId, seconds>`; `tickStatusEffects` (statusEffects.ts:98) counts them down and applies regen/poison. Each effect is read by exactly **one** seam (documented at statusEffects.ts:16): speed→playerMotion, strength→attack dispatch, haste→mining, resistance/jump_boost→their formulas, fire_resist/water_breathing→playerStats gates. Adding an effect = union + `EFFECT_ORDER` + one seam.

**Thrown-projectile machinery exists (arrows + spears):** `lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts` (`spawnArrow`) + `systems/projectileAI.ts` (`tickProjectiles`) — gravity-integrated, substepped swept collision against blocks and mobs/players, `fromPlayer` hit filter, delivers damage + knockback (projectileAI.ts:39). Spears are a parallel system (`systems/spears.ts`, `ThrownSpearState`). **Splash potions could reuse the arrow launch→tick→impact pattern**, but on-impact currently only does damage/knockback; a splash needs a new impact handler that calls `addEffect` on entities in a radius.

**Key friction for potions-on-mobs:** `MobState` (state.ts:100-146) has **no effects map** — only hp, direction, timers, faction. So applying a *lingering* effect to a mob has no storage seam. DOT-on-mobs today is done inline by decrementing hp per tick, with two precedents: daylight burn `mob.hp -= dt*0.8` (mobAI.ts:512) and fish suffocation `mob.hp -= FISH_SUFFOCATION_HP_PER_SECOND*dt` (mobAI.ts:248). A lingering fire/poison on a mob would need a new session-only timer field on `MobState`. Applying effects to *players* is easy (`addEffect` exists).

**Night Vision plug-in point:** `render/GameRenderer.ts:635-644`, the day/night lighting update (`sun.intensity`, `hemiLight.intensity`, sky lerp, all from `state.daylight`), plus the world material's daylight shader patch (~GameRenderer.ts:41). Night Vision = boost/clamp effective daylight (or add a brightness uniform) when the local player holds the effect. # Codebase state report: six systems

## 1. Vehicle system (rafts/ships)

**Files:** `lib/game/engine/systems/vehicles.ts` (all logic), `lib/game/render/vehicleVisuals.ts` (render), `VehicleState` in `lib/game/engine/state.ts:199`, config in `lib/game/config.ts:14-24`.

**Representation:** A vehicle is a **free entity with a float position**, not a block. `VehicleState = { id, kind, position: THREE.Vector3, yaw, rider: PlayerId | null }` (state.ts:199-205). They live in `state.vehicles: VehicleState[]` + `state.nextVehicleId` (state.ts:361). `VehicleKind = "raft" | "ship"` (types.ts:122); per-kind tuning via a `VEHICLE_SPECS` record (vehicles.ts:36).

**Boarding/riding:** `mountVehicle` sets `vehicle.rider = player.id` and `player.mountedVehicleId = vehicle.id` (vehicles.ts:135) — a bidirectional link. Two board paths: aimed raycast board (`tryBoardAimedVehicle`, VEHICLE_BOARD_REACH=4.5, vehicles.ts:205) and auto-board when walking onto a ship's deck (`tickVehicles` fallback loop, vehicles.ts:259). `syncPlayerToVehicle` snaps the rider to the boat, zeroes velocity, sets onGround, and player physics is skipped while mounted (vehicles.ts:176).

**Movement while mounted:** `tickVehicles` (vehicles.ts:238) reads `input.move`: forward/back = **direct position integration** along the yaw-forward vector (`position += forward * speed * dt`), NOT a physics force; left/right = yaw turn (VEHICLE_TURN_RATE); crouch = dismount. Every move is gated by `canOccupy` → `vehicleHasWaterSupport` (4 corners + center must be Water below and Air at deck) + in-bounds + no vehicle overlap (vehicles.ts:97-133). A blocked move is reverted to the previous position.

**Persistence:** Save field `vehicles?: SavedVehicle[]` added in save v16 (types.ts:351-356). `SavedVehicle = { kind, x, y, z, yaw }` (types.ts:315) — no id, no rider (rider is session-only). `serializeVehicles`/`restoreVehicles` (save.ts:357-374); `restoreVehicle` rebuilds unconditionally with no re-validation (vehicles.ts:55). `MAX_VEHICLES=64` bounds save size.

**Multiplayer (`vp` channel):** `VehiclePose = { id, kind, x, y, z, yaw, riderId }` (protocol.ts:127). Server owns mounted motion; `riderId` is cosmetic on clients. Full set ships in the sync snapshot (`vehicles: VehiclePose[]`, protocol.ts:117); per-tick `vp?` deltas carry only vehicles that moved past a deadband (`collectVehiclePoses`, room.ts:588, uses `MOB_DEADBAND_SQ` + quantized pos/ang). Client applies via `upsertReplicaVehicle` (NetworkSession.ts:356). Replicas early-return before world systems.

**Minecart reuse verdict — mostly yes on the plumbing, no on movement:**
- **Reusable as-is (kind-agnostic):** the rider link (`mountedVehicleId` ↔ `rider`), persistence (`SavedVehicle` + save field + cap), and replication (`vp`/`VehiclePose` deadband). Adding `"minecart"` to the `VehicleKind` union + a `VEHICLE_SPECS` entry gets you riding, saving, and netcode nearly free.
- **Must be rewritten per-kind:** movement and placement are hardcoded to water. `tickVehicles` does free WASD steering; `canOccupy`/`vehicleHasWaterSupport` require a water column; `tryPlaceVehicle` is gated on `slot.id === "raft"|"ship"` and a `waterSurfaceRaycast` (vehicles.ts:212-236). A rail-guided cart needs a rail-follow movement function and a rail/ground support check — these three functions would need a per-kind branch/strategy.
- **Net-new:** there is no rail block. Rails would need new BlockIds + a mesher shape (flat — the redstone-overlay pattern already proves this, see §3).

## 2. Redstone system ("redstone-lite")

**Files:** `lib/world/redstone.ts` (pure id helpers), `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.ts` (simulation), BlockIds in `lib/world/blocks.ts:87-104`, tunables in `config.ts:210-217`.

**Block ids (58-69):** RedstoneWire 58/On 59, Lever 60/On 61, RedstoneButton 62/On 63, PressurePlate 64/On 65, RedstoneTorchOff 66/RedstoneTorch(lit) 67, RedstoneLamp 68/LampOn 69.

**Power representation = id parity** (rides the block diff, exactly like doors): even=off, odd=on. `redstoneOn(b)=b|1`, `redstoneOff(b)=b&~1`, `isRedstoneOn=(b&1)===1` (redstone.ts world helpers). A toggle is a single `blockChanges.set` write that gets relight + save-diff + net-journal for free. **Power itself is never persisted** — `RedstoneState` (cells set, button timers, prevDoorPowered, timer) is session-only (state.ts:391) and re-derived from the grid every pass. Boot recovers the component set by scanning the block diff (`seedRedstoneCells`, redstone.ts:49 — works because every component is craft-only/player-placed).

**Tick:** `tickRedstone` at fixed `REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS=0.1` cadence (config.ts:213). Three phases (redstone.ts:123): (1) inputs & self-heal (pressure plates from occupied cells, button pop-back `REDSTONE_BUTTON_PRESS_SECONDS`, overlay-support checks), (2) power graph re-derived — sources power their 6 face neighbors, wire relaxes outward with a hop budget `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE=15` and ±1 slope climbing, (3) outputs written only on change (wire, lamp, torch-inverter). Runs server-side only; replicas receive the resulting block deltas.

**Powered-consumer seams (redstone.ts:267-299):** after computing the `powered` set, one loop dispatches on consumer block id: `Tnt` → `primeTnt` (idempotent), doors → `forceDoor` on rising/falling edge (tracked via `prevDoorPowered`). A **powered rail is easy** (a consumer that flips a block-id variant / gates cart motion). Placement/interact seams already exist: `trackRedstoneCell` (redstone.ts:56), and right-click handled in `interact.ts:91-92` (`toggleLever`/`pressButton`).

**Moving/pushing blocks anywhere: NONE.** No piston, no block-translation, no "block in motion" state anywhere in the codebase. **File:** `lib/world/meshing.ts` (`buildGeometryBuffers`).

**Default = full unit cube** with per-face culling (hidden faces skipped), baked AO in vertex colors, atlas UVs, split into opaque + glass layers (meshing.ts:249-299).

**Partial geometry IS a first-class pattern.** Two special cases route to `pushBlockCuboid` — an **arbitrary inset box** (min/max on all three axes) rendered with no neighbor culling:

- **Doors render as thin panels:** `doorBounds` = a 3/16-thick, full-height slab positioned per facing, rotating to the hinge edge when open (doors.ts:58-70; meshing.ts:255).

**Slabs/stairs/rails feasibility:** the inset-cuboid path already exists, so **slabs are trivial** (one half-height box) and **rails are trivial** (flat, exactly like wire). **Stairs** need two boxes — a small extension of the single-`pushBlockCuboid` pattern. Two caveats: (a) `pushBlockCuboid` draws all 6 faces uncconditionally (no culling), so a slab abutting a full block double-draws the shared face — a perf nit, not a blocker; (b) collision shape is separate — doors already carry a partial-AABB collision shape (`doorBounds`), so there's a template, but each new shape needs its own collision box (redstone overlays are deliberately non-colliding).

## 4. World/dimension model

**Single fixed volume.** `WORLD_SIZE_X=512, WORLD_SIZE_Y=150, WORLD_SIZE_Z=512` (blocks.ts:1-3). One `VoxelWorld` = a flat `Uint8Array(sizeX*sizeY*sizeZ)` block array + a parallel light array + a `seed` (voxelWorld.ts:15-33). `GameState.world` is a single instance; `state.mobs`, `state.containers`, `state.vehicles`, dungeon/village index sets are all keyed to that one world.

**Save = seed + block diff.** `SaveData` carries `seed: number` + `changes: Array<[number, number]>` — a sparse voxel-index→blockId diff over deterministically generated terrain (types.ts:146-147). Lighting is a derived cache (not saved); lava is worldgen (not saved). `WORLDGEN_VERSION=11` gates diff applicability (config.ts:390).

**Second dimension (Nether-like) is a substantial structural change.** It requires a **second VoxelWorld volume plus a second block-diff section** in the save, and dimension-keyed copies of mobs/containers/vehicles (all currently single-world in `GameState`). There is no existing "multiple co-existing worlds in one save" concept. (Note: there IS a multi-*world* feature in `lib/game/worlds.ts`, but those are separate save slots you load one at a time, not simultaneous dimensions.)

**Teleport/portal machinery: none for cross-space.** The only teleport-like code is `forceUnstuck` (GameEngine.ts:1598, nudges a wedged player to a safe cell) and pet recall (`PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE`, mobAI.ts:355). Spectator/Creative **noclip** (`isNoclip`, gameModes.ts:64) is free movement through blocks but stays in the same world. No portal block, no dimension transition, no "move player + swap world" seam — all net-new.

**Buckets: DO NOT EXIST.** No bucket item; no water/lava pickup or source placement anywhere (the only `bucket` matches are an unrelated recipe-bucketing helper in recipes.ts). Water (17) and Lava (47) are blocks, but Lava is worldgen-only and unmineable, and there's no item that scoops or places a fluid source. Fluid pickup/placement is net-new.

## 5. Status effects / potions and combat seams

**Effect definitions:** `EffectId` union (types.ts:12) = `speed | strength | regeneration | fire_resistance | water_breathing | haste | resistance | jump_boost | poison`. Each effect is read by exactly **one** seam (documented at statusEffects.ts:16): speed→playerMotion, strength→attack dispatch, haste→mining, resistance/jump_boost→their formulas, fire_resist/water_breathing→playerStats gates. Adding an effect = union + `EFFECT_ORDER` + one seam.

**Thrown-projectile machinery exists (arrows + spears):** `lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts` (`spawnArrow`) + `systems/projectileAI.ts` (`tickProjectiles`) — gravity-integrated, substepped swept collision against blocks and mobs/players, `fromPlayer` hit filter, delivers damage + knockback (projectileAI.ts:39). **Key friction for potions-on-mobs:** `MobState` (state.ts:100-146) has **no effects map** — only hp, direction, timers, faction. So applying a *lingering* effect to a mob has no storage seam. DOT-on-mobs today is done inline by decrementing hp per tick, with two precedents: daylight burn `mob.hp -= dt*0.8` (mobAI.ts:512) and fish suffocation `mob.hp -= FISH_SUFFOCATION_HP_PER_SECOND*dt` (mobAI.ts:248). ## 6. Ocean/hostile gaps

# PR 1 — Rails & minecarts (`feat/rails-minecarts`)

## Goal

Craftable rail tracks (plain, powered, detector) as flat non-colliding floor overlays riding the existing redstone machinery, plus a `"minecart"` `VehicleKind` that snaps to rails, is ridden like a raft, is boosted/braked by powered rails, and trips detector rails as a redstone source. Everything persists via the existing block diff + `vehicles` save field; multiplayer works through the existing `vp` channel with no protocol bump.

## Key design decisions (with recommendations)

1. **Rail set: plain + powered + detector, flat-only.** Include the detector rail — it's cheap (the pressure-plate pattern already exists in `tickRedstone` phase 1: occupancy → parity toggle → phase-2 source) and it's what makes rails a *redstone* feature (cart-triggered doors/lamps/TNT traps). **Defer slopes entirely** — no 1-block climbing rails. Rationale: slope rails would need cart pitch, gravity acceleration, sloped overlay meshing, and slope-aware pathing; flat tracks + powered boosts deliver 90% of the fun. Corners/T-junctions: **supported implicitly by pathing, not by dedicated curve blocks** (see 3).
2. **No orientation encoding in BlockIds — orientation is derived from neighbors.** Unlike doors (16 ids for one door), rails follow the *wire* precedent: one id per rail type, connectivity derived from the grid. The mesher already reads neighbors; the rail overlay branch checks "is east or west neighbor a rail?" to orient the painted strips E–W vs N–S (a corner cell just picks its dominant axis — cosmetically fine at this art resolution). This saves 8+ ids, needs no placement-facing logic, and self-heals as track is extended (placing a rail sets `worldMeshDirty`, the remesh reorients neighbors for free). Two atlas tiles (or one tile rotated by swapping UV axes in the overlay branch) per rail type.
3. **Cart pathing: cell-hopping along the rail graph.** Cart state = position (snapped to the rail centerline, `y = railY + 0.1`), heading axis, and a session-only `speed` scalar (additive optional field on `VehicleState`; never serialized — parked carts restore at rest, matching `SavedVehicle`'s kind/pose-only shape). Each tick: advance along heading by `speed·dt`; on crossing a cell boundary, prefer the straight-ahead rail, else turn to a perpendicular neighbor rail (this **is** the corner support — an L of rails just works), else stop at track end. If the cell under the cart stops being a rail (mined out), the cart parks inert — the `restoreVehicle` "beached boat" philosophy, gated by a new per-kind `vehicleHasSupport`.
4. **Drive model: rider-accelerated + powered-rail boost.** Forward input accelerates toward `MINECART_SPEED`, back brakes/reverses, plain rail applies mild friction, `PoweredRailOn` accelerates toward `MINECART_BOOST_SPEED`, `PoweredRail` (off) is a hard brake (MC semantics — an unpowered powered-rail is a stopper). Riderless carts **coast** under the same friction/boost rules, so a button-powered launcher track works. Yaw snaps to the heading axis.
5. **Riderless coasting ticks once per frame, world-scoped.** New `tickCoastingMinecarts(state, dt)` exported from `vehicles.ts`, called from `GameEngine.step` beside `tickMobs` (after the player loop). The per-player `tickVehicles` handles only the *mounted* cart (each player has ≤1). This is the correctness catch flagged above — do not put coasting in the per-player path.
6. **Placement/boarding**: `tryPlaceVehicle` gains a `minecart` branch: normal `voxelRaycast` (rails are `isSolid`, so the ray hits the rail cell), require `isRailBlock(world.get(hit))`, spawn centered on the cell. Boarding reuses `tryBoardAimedVehicle` unchanged (VEHICLE_SPECS is `Record<VehicleKind, …>` — typecheck forces the minecart spec entry). Dismount = crouch, reusing `dismountVehicle`'s spec-driven offsets. No step-on auto-board (that's a ship behavior).
7. **Redstone integration**:
   - All five rail ids are **tracked cells**: extend `seedRedstoneCells`/placement tracking/phase-1 self-heal with `isRailBlock` so rails get support-pop for free (works because rails are craft-only → always in the block diff — the `seedRedstoneCells` invariant holds).
   - `DetectorRailOn` when a minecart occupies the cell: phase 1 computes cart-occupied indices from `state.vehicles` (kind minecart, `floor(position)`) and toggles parity exactly like plates; `DetectorRailOn` joins the phase-2 source list. (Bonus: adding cart cells to `collectOccupiedCells` also lets carts press pressure plates — recommend yes, it's one line and it's fun.)
   - `PoweredRail` is a **level-triggered output** like the lamp: phase 3, `on = powered.has(index)`.
   - The family predicates: `isRedstoneBlock` becomes `(58..69) || isPoweredRail(b) || isDetectorRail(b)`; `redstoneOn/Off` parity math is id-agnostic and works on 70–73 as-is. Plain `Rail` (74) is **not** a redstone block (parity math must never touch it) but **is** tracked and **is** an overlay for meshing/collision/lighting.
8. **Recipes** (gold gates redstone, sliver is the iron analog — matches the existing economy): `3 sliver_ore + 3 wood → 16 rail`; `2 gold_ore + 1 redstone + 2 wood → 4 powered_rail`; `1 sliver_ore + 1 redstone + 1 cobble → 2 detector_rail`; `5 sliver_ore → 1 minecart`. Rails are `kind: "block"` → auto-bucketed into **Building**; minecart is `kind: "vehicle"` → **Vehicles**. 
9. **No save bump, no worldgen bump, no protocol bump** (statement below).

# PR 2 — The drowned (`feat/drowned`)

## Goal

A hostile aquatic mob that makes night oceans dangerous: spawns underwater near players at night (difficulty-gated), pursues and melees players in/at the water in 3D, stays strictly water-bound, drops kelp/rotten flesh and rarely a sliver spear. No new blocks, no save/worldgen/protocol impact.

## Key design decisions

1. **Strictly water-bound** (recommended): the pursue move stays gated on "destination cell is Water" — the same gate that keeps fish in water automatically keeps the drowned from ever emerging, with zero extra code. Beached (knockback onto land) → reuse the fish suffocation branch. This is the tight-scope answer; land-walking drowned would need the entire land-hostile branch merged into the aquatic tick.
2. **Combat lives inside `tickAquaticMob`** as a `template.aquatic && mob.hostile` branch (the aquatic early-`continue` at `mobAI.ts:297` means the land combat loop can never serve it): target `nearestTargetablePlayer`; if within `detectRange`, steer 3D toward the player's eye (speed ×1.15) instead of fleeing; strike when 3D distance < `DROWNED_MELEE_REACH` with an `attackTimer` cooldown, LOS raycast (`voxelRaycast` treats water as empty — works underwater), `deps.damagePlayer(hunted, attackDamage × mobDamageMultiplier)` + the standard knockback shove. Players merely *near* water (on a boat, on the beach edge) are reachable only within melee reach of a water cell — emergent and fine.

## Key design decisions

1. **Bottom-only slabs, no double-slab merging** (recommended): top-half slabs double the id budget and add placement-face logic; bottom slabs deliver the building value. Documented deferral.
2. **Stair facing in the BlockId, doors-style**: 4 contiguous ids per material, decoded by offset math in a new `lib/world/slabs.ts` (or `shapes.ts`): `isSlabBlock` (75..77), `isStairBlock` (78..89), `stairState(block) → {facing}`, `stairBlock(materialBase, facing)`. 3. **Meshing = uncculled cuboids, two per stair**: slab → one `pushBlockCuboid(…, minY 0, maxY 0.5)`; stair → bottom half full-cell + top half with the facing half's X/Z bounds (a small `stairBoxes(block)` helper returning 1–2 boxes shared by mesher and collision — the `doorBounds` pattern generalized to Y). Perf note: uncculled boxes cost more triangles than culled cubes, but these are hand-placed decorative blocks (the doors/redstone precedent) — acceptable; noted in docs.
4. **Collision gets its first partial-Y branch**: in `collidesAt`, for each candidate box (slab = one, stair = two) test full 3D AABB overlap: X/Z door-style plus `bodyMinY < y + box.maxY && bodyMaxY > y + box.minY`. Mobs share `collidesAt`, so mob collision is automatic.
5. **Auto-step is the load-bearing new mechanic — build it deliberately.** In `tickPlayerMotion.stepAxis` (x/z only), when a step collides and the player was grounded: probe `position + step + (0, STEP_UP_HEIGHT, 0)`; if clear, additionally probe back down to find the landing (≤ `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` above the old foot level) and commit; else revert as today. Constraints verified: server pose clamp tolerates a 0.5 rise per tick (`+0.6` slack); flying/noclip skip it naturally (their branch bypasses); crouch edge-guard runs after and still protects edges; **this also makes single full blocks climbable — gate the step height to 0.55 so full-block auto-step also works (a deliberate feel upgrade, MC parity) — or clamp to 0.51 to keep it slab/stair-only. 7. **Support rules**: slabs/stairs are NOT valid support for doors/redstone/rails — extend the shared support predicate in `mining.placeSelectedBlock`, `redstone.ts` phase 1, and PR 1's rail placement (the doors-exclusion precedent; `world.isSolid` alone would accept them and leave floaters).
8. **Lighting: keep the default (opaque)** — zero `lighting.ts` change, matching the doors precedent. A slab roof casts full shade; documented, revisitable.
9. **Placement on/against slabs**: no special casing — the raycast targets the slab cell, `previous` is the neighbor, standard placement. Placing a block "on" a slab puts it in the cell above (a visible half-gap) — MC bottom-slab behavior, accepted.
10. **Recipes**: `3 planks → 6 plank_slab`, `3 stone → 6 stone_slab`, `3 cobble → 6 cobble_slab`; `6 planks → 4 plank_stairs`, etc. `kind: "block"` → **Building** category automatically.

# PR 1 — Rails & minecarts (`feat/rails-minecarts`)

## Goal

Craftable rail tracks (plain, powered, detector) as flat non-colliding floor overlays riding the existing redstone machinery, plus a `"minecart"` `VehicleKind` that snaps to rails, is ridden like a raft, is boosted/braked by powered rails, and trips detector rails as a redstone source. Everything persists via the existing block diff + `vehicles` save field; multiplayer works through the existing `vp` channel with no protocol bump.

## Key design decisions (with recommendations)

1. **Rail set: plain + powered + detector, flat-only.** Include the detector rail — it's cheap (the pressure-plate pattern already exists in `tickRedstone` phase 1: occupancy → parity toggle → phase-2 source) and it's what makes rails a *redstone* feature (cart-triggered doors/lamps/TNT traps). **Defer slopes entirely** — no 1-block climbing rails. Rationale: slope rails would need cart pitch, gravity acceleration, sloped overlay meshing, and slope-aware pathing; flat tracks + powered boosts deliver 90% of the fun. Corners/T-junctions: **supported implicitly by pathing, not by dedicated curve blocks** (see 3).
2. **No orientation encoding in BlockIds — orientation is derived from neighbors.** Unlike doors (16 ids for one door), rails follow the *wire* precedent: one id per rail type, connectivity derived from the grid. The mesher already reads neighbors; the rail overlay branch checks "is east or west neighbor a rail?" to orient the painted strips E–W vs N–S (a corner cell just picks its dominant axis — cosmetically fine at this art resolution). This saves 8+ ids, needs no placement-facing logic, and self-heals as track is extended (placing a rail sets `worldMeshDirty`, the remesh reorients neighbors for free). Two atlas tiles (or one tile rotated by swapping UV axes in the overlay branch) per rail type.
3. **Cart pathing: cell-hopping along the rail graph.** Cart state = position (snapped to the rail centerline, `y = railY + 0.1`), heading axis, and a session-only `speed` scalar (additive optional field on `VehicleState`; never serialized — parked carts restore at rest, matching `SavedVehicle`'s kind/pose-only shape). Each tick: advance along heading by `speed·dt`; on crossing a cell boundary, prefer the straight-ahead rail, else turn to a perpendicular neighbor rail (this **is** the corner support — an L of rails just works), else stop at track end. If the cell under the cart stops being a rail (mined out), the cart parks inert — the `restoreVehicle` "beached boat" philosophy, gated by a new per-kind `vehicleHasSupport`.
4. **Drive model: rider-accelerated + powered-rail boost.** Forward input accelerates toward `MINECART_SPEED`, back brakes/reverses, plain rail applies mild friction, `PoweredRailOn` accelerates toward `MINECART_BOOST_SPEED`, `PoweredRail` (off) is a hard brake (MC semantics — an unpowered powered-rail is a stopper). Riderless carts **coast** under the same friction/boost rules, so a button-powered launcher track works. Yaw snaps to the heading axis.
5. **Riderless coasting ticks once per frame, world-scoped.** New `tickCoastingMinecarts(state, dt)` exported from `vehicles.ts`, called from `GameEngine.step` beside `tickMobs` (after the player loop). The per-player `tickVehicles` handles only the *mounted* cart (each player has ≤1). This is the correctness catch flagged above — do not put coasting in the per-player path.
6. **Placement/boarding**: `tryPlaceVehicle` gains a `minecart` branch: normal `voxelRaycast` (rails are `isSolid`, so the ray hits the rail cell), require `isRailBlock(world.get(hit))`, spawn centered on the cell. Boarding reuses `tryBoardAimedVehicle` unchanged (VEHICLE_SPECS is `Record<VehicleKind, …>` — typecheck forces the minecart spec entry). Dismount = crouch, reusing `dismountVehicle`'s spec-driven offsets. No step-on auto-board (that's a ship behavior).
7. **Redstone integration**:
   - All five rail ids are **tracked cells**: extend `seedRedstoneCells`/placement tracking/phase-1 self-heal with `isRailBlock` so rails get support-pop for free (works because rails are craft-only → always in the block diff — the `seedRedstoneCells` invariant holds).
   - `DetectorRailOn` when a minecart occupies the cell: phase 1 computes cart-occupied indices from `state.vehicles` (kind minecart, `floor(position)`) and toggles parity exactly like plates; `DetectorRailOn` joins the phase-2 source list. (Bonus: adding cart cells to `collectOccupiedCells` also lets carts press pressure plates — recommend yes, it's one line and it's fun.)
   - `PoweredRail` is a **level-triggered output** like the lamp: phase 3, `on = powered.has(index)`.
   - The family predicates: `isRedstoneBlock` becomes `(58..69) || isPoweredRail(b) || isDetectorRail(b)`; `redstoneOn/Off` parity math is id-agnostic and works on 70–73 as-is. Plain `Rail` (74) is **not** a redstone block (parity math must never touch it) but **is** tracked and **is** an overlay for meshing/collision/lighting.
8. **Recipes** (gold gates redstone, sliver is the iron analog — matches the existing economy): `3 sliver_ore + 3 wood → 16 rail`; `2 gold_ore + 1 redstone + 2 wood → 4 powered_rail`; `1 sliver_ore + 1 redstone + 1 cobble → 2 detector_rail`; `5 sliver_ore → 1 minecart`. Rails are `kind: "block"` → auto-bucketed into **Building**; minecart is `kind: "vehicle"` → **Vehicles**. 
9. **No save bump, no worldgen bump, no protocol bump** (statement below).

# PR 2 — The drowned (`feat/drowned`)

## Goal

A hostile aquatic mob that makes night oceans dangerous: spawns underwater near players at night (difficulty-gated), pursues and melees players in/at the water in 3D, stays strictly water-bound, drops kelp/rotten flesh and rarely a sliver spear. No new blocks, no save/worldgen/protocol impact.

## Key design decisions

1. **Strictly water-bound** (recommended): the pursue move stays gated on "destination cell is Water" — the same gate that keeps fish in water automatically keeps the drowned from ever emerging, with zero extra code. Beached (knockback onto land) → reuse the fish suffocation branch. This is the tight-scope answer; land-walking drowned would need the entire land-hostile branch merged into the aquatic tick.
2. **Combat lives inside `tickAquaticMob`** as a `template.aquatic && mob.hostile` branch (the aquatic early-`continue` at `mobAI.ts:297` means the land combat loop can never serve it): target `nearestTargetablePlayer`; if within `detectRange`, steer 3D toward the player's eye (speed ×1.15) instead of fleeing; strike when 3D distance < `DROWNED_MELEE_REACH` with an `attackTimer` cooldown, LOS raycast (`voxelRaycast` treats water as empty — works underwater), `deps.damagePlayer(hunted, attackDamage × mobDamageMultiplier)` + the standard knockback shove. Players merely *near* water (on a boat, on the beach edge) are reachable only within melee reach of a water cell — emergent and fine.
3. **No daylight burn** (it's submerged — thematically shielded; also the burn check lives in the land branch it never reaches). Peaceful despawn, HOSTILE_CAP membership, and difficulty damage scaling all come free from `hostile: true`.
4. **Spawning: extend `tickAquaticSpawnDirector`** (recommended over a new director — it already owns the water sampler and cadence): after the passive top-up, a night-gated hostile branch — `hostilesSpawn(difficulty) && daylight < HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`, its own `DROWNED_CAP` (count `aquatic && hostile`) **and** the global hostile cap × `hostileCapScale`, interval scaled by `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`. Two sampler changes: `spawnAquaticGroup` gains a `hostile` flag (currently hardcodes `false`), and `randomWaterPointNear` gains an optional `minRadius` (mirror `randomLandPointNear`) so a drowned can't materialize point-blank under a swimming player. **Fix the passive-cap count** to `aquatic && !hostile` so drowned don't starve the fish population against `AQUATIC_CAP`. No day-one drowned in `spawnInitialMobs`.
5. **Drops** (all existing items): `rotten_flesh` 1–2 (zombie kinship), `kelp` 0–1, **`sliver_spear` at ~7% chance** — the trident nod; a chance-gated durable weapon drop is a first, but `rollMobDrops` → `tryInsertSlots` handles durables fine (`createSlot` initializes durability). XP: same as zombie's `MOB_XP` value.
6. **Model**: zombie silhouette in drowned teal — `createMobModel` default `"quadruped"` variant with tall body args (copy zombie's `[0.78, 1.1, 0.52]` shape, palette ~`0x3f8a7a/0x2f6f63` with cyan `0x66ffd9` eyes). It stands on animated legs underwater — acceptable at this art level (fish are the only legless variant; a "swimmer humanoid" variant is deferred).
7. **Sounds**: gurgly-zombie `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`/`MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` rows (ZZFX designer pass), `CALL_INTERVALS` ~[6, 14].
8. **Advancement**: `recordEvent` already buckets any `mobDied` with a `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` member into `hostiles_killed`; add a dedicated `drowned_killed` bump on `mobDied` kind `"drowned"` and an `ADVANCEMENTS` row `{ id: "ocean_purge", title: "Revenge of the Tides", icon: "sliver_spear", stat: "drowned_killed", threshold: 1 }`.
9. **Multiplayer: zero net code.** Mobs replicate by pose channel keyed on the kind string; both builds share `MOB_TEMPLATES`, so the replica's `mobVisuals` renders it via `createMobModelForKind` unchanged.

# PR 3 — Slabs & stairs (`feat/slabs-stairs`)

## Goal

Six craft-only building families — plank/stone/cobble slabs (bottom-half) and stairs (4 facings each) — with correct partial collision, **auto-step so walking up them needs no jump**, two-box stair meshing, yaw-derived stair facing, and classic recipes. Ids 75–89.

## Key design decisions

1. **Bottom-only slabs, no double-slab merging** (recommended): top-half slabs double the id budget and add placement-face logic; bottom slabs deliver the building value. Documented deferral.
2. **Stair facing in the BlockId, doors-style**: 4 contiguous ids per material, decoded by offset math in a new `lib/world/slabs.ts` (or `shapes.ts`): `isSlabBlock` (75..77), `isStairBlock` (78..89), `stairState(block) → {facing}`, `stairBlock(materialBase, facing)`. Facing derives from player yaw at placement — **reuse `doorFacingFromYaw` verbatim** (exported from `doors.ts`); recommend stairs face *toward* the player (ascending away), matching MC.
3. **Meshing = uncculled cuboids, two per stair**: slab → one `pushBlockCuboid(…, minY 0, maxY 0.5)`; stair → bottom half full-cell + top half with the facing half's X/Z bounds (a small `stairBoxes(block)` helper returning 1–2 boxes shared by mesher and collision — the `doorBounds` pattern generalized to Y). Add `isSlabBlock/isStairBlock` to the neighbor-culling exemption in `buildGeometryBuffers` (line 275) so adjacent full cubes keep their faces. Perf note: uncculled boxes cost more triangles than culled cubes, but these are hand-placed decorative blocks (the doors/redstone precedent) — acceptable; noted in docs.
4. **Collision gets its first partial-Y branch**: in `collidesAt`, for each candidate box (slab = one, stair = two) test full 3D AABB overlap: X/Z door-style plus `bodyMinY < y + box.maxY && bodyMaxY > y + box.minY`. Mobs share `collidesAt`, so mob collision is automatic.
5. **Auto-step is the load-bearing new mechanic — build it deliberately.** In `tickPlayerMotion.stepAxis` (x/z only), when a step collides and the player was grounded: probe `position + step + (0, STEP_UP_HEIGHT, 0)`; if clear, additionally probe back down to find the landing (≤ `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` above the old foot level) and commit; else revert as today. Constraints verified: server pose clamp tolerates a 0.5 rise per tick (`+0.6` slack); flying/noclip skip it naturally (their branch bypasses); crouch edge-guard runs after and still protects edges; **this also makes single full blocks climbable — gate the step height to 0.55 so full-block auto-step also works (a deliberate feel upgrade, MC parity) — or clamp to 0.51 to keep it slab/stair-only. Recommend 0.55 + MC-parity full-block stepping, called out in the CHANGELOG as a movement change.** New unit tests must pin: step up a slab, step up a stair, NOT step up a 2-block wall, no mid-air stepping, no step while crouch-edge-guarded.

**Commits**: (1) `feat(mobs)` drowned kind — tables/loot/xp/sounds; (2) `feat(engine)` aquatic hostile AI + night ocean spawning; (3) `feat(progress)` stat/advancement + `docs`.

**Tests**: `mobAI.test.ts` (pursues, never leaves water, strikes with difficulty scaling, ignores Creative, suffocates beached), `spawnDirector.test.ts` (night gate, Peaceful no-op, caps, dry-world fails closed, fish cap unaffected, minRadius), `mobLoot.test.ts` (spear chance bounds), headless `GameEngine` night-spawn probe. Plank/stone/cobble slabs (bottom-half only) + stairs (4 facings), with the first partial-Y collision and a new **auto-step** mechanic.

- **Bottom-only slabs**, no double-slab merging (deferred). Stair facing encoded in BlockId, doors-style; facing derived from player yaw at placement — reuse `doorFacingFromYaw` from `doors.ts`.

# Next features: Rails & Minecarts + Drowned + Slabs & Stairs (one branch, one PR)

## Context

Redstone-lite just merged (PR #57). Asked "what next?", we surveyed the deferred-feature list against the current code. Three directions were picked (Nether stays parked — it's genuinely structural: single-world save/GameState, no buckets/portals). All three need **no save bump (stays v17), no worldgen bump (stays 11), no protocol bump (stays 3)** — craft-only appended BlockIds, transient hostiles, and an additive `VehicleKind` riding the existing `vehicles` save field and `vp` net channel.

**Delivery shape (user-decided): ONE branch `feat/rails-drowned-slabs` off `main`, ONE PR, ~13 focused commits** — three contiguous commit groups in order (rails/minecarts → drowned → slabs/stairs), each group reading like a mini-PR, precedent PR #23 (content expansion) and #42 (aquatic update). This also removes the cross-feature friction: rails and slabs/stairs touch the same overlay-support predicate (`mining.ts`/`redstone.ts`), and BlockIds 70–89 allocate linearly on one branch. Each feature gets its own CHANGELOG entry; the auto-step movement change gets its own clearly-flagged commit so it isn't buried in the diff.

Exploration confirmed the big feasibility facts:
- Vehicle riding/persistence/replication is kind-agnostic (`lib/game/engine/systems/vehicles.ts`, `SavedVehicle`, `VehiclePose`); only movement/placement is water-hardcoded.
- The mesher has a first-class partial-shape path (`pushBlockCuboid` in `lib/world/meshing.ts` — redstone wire is a real flat slab, doors are thin panels); it can be called multiple times per block (stairs = two boxes).
- Redstone consumers are a one-branch seam (`lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.ts` phase 3 / consumer loop); sources like the pressure plate are the detector-rail template.
- `tickAquaticMob` (mobAI.ts) already solves water-confined 3D movement; it has zero combat (aquatic mobs `continue` before land-hostile logic).
- **No auto-step exists** in `playerMotion.ts` `stepAxis` — walking into a 0.5 rise stops you dead. This is the hidden hard part of slabs/stairs.
- `isRedstoneBlock` is a contiguous 58..69 range check (`lib/world/redstone.ts:17`) — rails extend the predicate; parity pairs must start on even ids. Plain Rail must NEVER pass through `redstoneOn/Off` parity math.

**BlockId allocation:** 70 PoweredRail / 71 PoweredRailOn / 72 DetectorRail / 73 DetectorRailOn / 74 Rail; 75–77 Plank/Stone/Cobble Slab; 78–89 Plank/Stone/Cobble Stairs ×4 facings (N/E/S/W). Parity pairs (70/71, 72/73) start even — required by the redstone id-parity math.

---

## Feature group 1 — Rails & minecarts (flagship, commits 1–6)

Craftable rails (plain + powered + detector) as flat non-colliding floor overlays, plus a rideable `"minecart"` VehicleKind that follows rails, is boosted by powered rails, and trips detector rails as a redstone source.

**Key decisions**
- **Flat rails only** (no slopes — deferred). No orientation BlockIds: connectivity/orientation derived from neighbors like wire (`railAxis(world,x,y,z)` picks E–W vs N–S; corners work via pathing, not curve blocks).
- **Cart movement**: cell-hopping along the rail graph. Session-only `speed?: number` on `VehicleState` (never serialized — parked carts restore at rest). Per tick: advance along heading; at cell boundary prefer straight, else perpendicular neighbor rail (= corner support), else stop. Rail mined under a cart → cart parks inert (per-kind `vehicleHasSupport`).
- **Drive model**: forward input accelerates toward `MINECART_SPEED`, back brakes; `PoweredRailOn` boosts toward `MINECART_BOOST_SPEED`; unpowered `PoweredRail` = hard brake (MC semantics); plain rail mild friction. Riderless carts coast — **world-scoped `tickCoastingMinecarts(state, dt)` called once per frame from `GameEngine.step`** (NOT the per-player `tickVehicles` path, which runs once per player and would integrate N× in co-op). Call it before `tickRedstone` so detectors see this frame's positions.
- **Redstone**: all 5 rail ids are tracked cells (extend `seedRedstoneCells` + phase-1 self-heal/support-pop with `isRailBlock`). Detector = pressure-plate pattern (phase-1 occupancy from minecart cells → parity toggle; `DetectorRailOn` joins phase-2 sources). Powered rail = lamp pattern (phase-3 level output). Extend `isRedstoneBlock` with ids 70–73 only. Also add cart cells to `collectOccupiedCells` (carts press pressure plates — one line).
- **Placement/boarding**: `tryPlaceVehicle` minecart branch requires aiming at a rail block; boarding reuses `tryBoardAimedVehicle` (typecheck forces the `VEHICLE_SPECS.minecart` entry); crouch dismounts.
- **Recipes**: `3 sliver_ore + 3 wood → 16 rail`; `2 gold_ore + 1 redstone + 2 wood → 4 powered_rail`; `1 sliver_ore + 1 redstone + 1 cobble → 2 detector_rail`; `5 sliver_ore → 1 minecart` (Vehicles category; rails auto-bucket into Building).

**Files**: `lib/world/blocks.ts` (ids 70–74 + colors), **new `lib/world/rails.ts`** (predicates, `railBounds` flat box, `railAxis`), `lib/world/redstone.ts` (extend `isRedstoneBlock`), `meshing.ts` (rail overlay branch + culling exemption + UV orientation), `atlas.ts` (rail paint), `queries.ts` (non-colliding), `voxelWorld.ts` `highestSolidY` + `lighting.ts` opacity (overlay exemptions), `lib/game/types.ts` (`VehicleKind` + `"minecart"`), `engine/state.ts` (`speed?`, `vehicleBoarded`/`detectorToggled` events), `systems/vehicles.ts` (spec, per-kind support, minecart tick branch, `tickCoastingMinecarts`, placement branch), `GameEngine.ts` (coasting call), `systems/redstone.ts` (3 seams above), `systems/mining.ts` (rail support/pop-off + placement rule), `save.ts` (`VALID_VEHICLE_KINDS.minecart`), `items.ts`/`recipes.ts`/`spritePixels.ts` (MINECART_GRID), `render/vehicleVisuals.ts` (`createMinecart`, kind switch), `audio/materials.ts` + `soundParams.ts`/`audioDirector.ts` (rolling clack via footsteps-style accumulator; board/detector one-shots), `systems/advancements.ts` ("On Rails" — first minecart ride), `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` (`upsertReplicaVehicle` kind decode keeps `"minecart"`). Server `room.ts` needs nothing.

**Tunables**: `MINECART_SPEED` ~6, `MINECART_BOOST_SPEED` ~11, `MINECART_ACCEL`, `MINECART_FRICTION`, `MINECART_BRAKE_DECEL`, half-extents, ride height.

**Commits**: (1) `feat(world)` rail blocks/meshing/bounds; (2) `feat(items)` items+recipes+sprites; (3) `feat(engine)` minecart kind — rail following, placement, coasting tick; (4) `feat(engine)` rails join the redstone pass; (5) `feat(render,audio)` visuals+sounds+advancement; (6) `docs`.

**Tests**: new `lib/world/rails.test.ts`, **new `vehicles.test.ts`** (place/board/run/corner/track-end/mined-rail-park/boost-brake/coasting-once-with-2-players), `redstone.test.ts` (detector powers lamp; lever flips powered rail; support pop), `queries/save/GameEngine.multiplayer` extensions. e2e: smoke extension (creative-place rail+cart, assert vehicle kind + render).

---

## Feature group 2 — The drowned (smallest, commits 7–9)

Hostile aquatic mob: night oceans become dangerous. No new blocks; zero net code (mobs replicate by kind string).

**Key decisions**
- **Strictly water-bound**: pursue moves stay gated on destination-cell=Water (the fish gate) — never emerges onto land; beached → existing suffocation branch. No daylight burn (submerged; the burn check lives in the land branch anyway).
- **Combat inside `tickAquaticMob`** as an `aquatic && hostile` branch: `nearestTargetablePlayer`, 3D pursuit at ~1.15× speed within `detectRange`, strike when < `DROWNED_MELEE_REACH` with cooldown + LOS raycast, difficulty-scaled damage + knockback.
- **Spawning**: extend `tickAquaticSpawnDirector` with a night-gated hostile branch (`hostilesSpawn(difficulty)` + `HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`, own `DROWNED_CAP` + global hostile cap scaling). `spawnAquaticGroup` gains a `hostile` param (currently hardcodes false); `randomWaterPointNear` gains optional `minRadius` (mirror `randomLandPointNear`) so nothing materializes under a swimmer. **Fix passive fish cap count to `aquatic && !hostile`** so drowned don't starve fish against `AQUATIC_CAP`.
- **New MobKind fills all 7 exhaustive tables**: `MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND` (hostile), `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` + `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS`.
- **Drops**: rotten_flesh 1–2, kelp 0–1, **sliver_spear at ~7%** (the trident nod; `rollMobDrops`→`tryInsertSlots` handles durables). Zombie-tier XP. Model: tall zombie silhouette in drowned teal via `createMobModel` (legless swimmer variant deferred). Advancement: "Revenge of the Tides" (first drowned kill).

**Files**: `types.ts` (MobKind), `mobs.ts`, `mobAI.ts`, `spawnDirector.ts`, `spawn.ts`, `mobLoot.ts`, `mobXp.ts`, `audio/soundParams.ts` + `mobAmbience.ts`, `advancements.ts`, `config.ts`.

## Feature group 2 — The drowned (smallest, commits 7–9)

Hostile aquatic mob: night oceans become dangerous. No new blocks; zero net code (mobs replicate by kind string).

**Key decisions**
- **Strictly water-bound**: pursue moves stay gated on destination-cell=Water (the fish gate) — never emerges onto land; beached → existing suffocation branch. No daylight burn (submerged; the burn check lives in the land branch anyway).
- **Combat inside `tickAquaticMob`** as an `aquatic && hostile` branch: `nearestTargetablePlayer`, 3D pursuit at ~1.15× speed within `detectRange`, strike when < `DROWNED_MELEE_REACH` with cooldown + LOS raycast, difficulty-scaled damage + knockback.
- **Spawning**: extend `tickAquaticSpawnDirector` with a night-gated hostile branch (`hostilesSpawn(difficulty)` + `HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`, own `DROWNED_CAP` + global hostile cap scaling). `spawnAquaticGroup` gains a `hostile` param (currently hardcodes false); `randomWaterPointNear` gains optional `minRadius` (mirror `randomLandPointNear`) so nothing materializes under a swimmer. **Fix passive fish cap count to `aquatic && !hostile`** so drowned don't starve fish against `AQUATIC_CAP`.
- **New MobKind fills all 7 exhaustive tables**: `MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND` (hostile), `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` + `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS`.
- **Drops**: rotten_flesh 1–2, kelp 0–1, **sliver_spear at ~7%** (the trident nod; `rollMobDrops`→`tryInsertSlots` handles durables). Zombie-tier XP. Model: tall zombie silhouette in drowned teal via `createMobModel` (legless swimmer variant deferred). Advancement: "Revenge of the Tides" (first drowned kill).

**Files**: `types.ts` (MobKind), `mobs.ts`, `mobAI.ts`, `spawnDirector.ts`, `spawn.ts`, `mobLoot.ts`, `mobXp.ts`, `audio/soundParams.ts` + `mobAmbience.ts`, `advancements.ts`, `config.ts`.

**Tunables**: `DROWNED_CAP` 6, `DROWNED_MELEE_REACH` 1.9, `DROWNED_SPAWN_MIN_RADIUS` 10, spawn chance.

**Commits**: (1) `feat(mobs)` drowned kind — tables/loot/xp/sounds; (2) `feat(engine)` aquatic hostile AI + night ocean spawning; (3) `feat(progress)` stat/advancement + `docs`.

**Tests**: `mobAI.test.ts` (pursues, never leaves water, strikes with difficulty scaling, ignores Creative, suffocates beached), `spawnDirector.test.ts` (night gate, Peaceful no-op, caps, dry-world fails closed, fish cap unaffected, minRadius), `mobLoot.test.ts` (spear chance bounds), headless `GameEngine` night-spawn probe. No e2e needed.

---

## Feature group 3 — Slabs & stairs (commits 10–13)

Plank/stone/cobble slabs (bottom-half only) + stairs (4 facings), with the first partial-Y collision and a new **auto-step** mechanic.

**Key decisions**
- **Bottom-only slabs**, no double-slab merging (deferred). Stair facing encoded in BlockId, doors-style; facing derived from player yaw at placement — reuse `doorFacingFromYaw` from `doors.ts`.
- **New `lib/world/slabs.ts`** (doors.ts sibling): predicates, `slabBox`/`stairBoxes(block)` returning 1–2 boxes **shared by mesher and collision**. Mesher: 1–2 `pushBlockCuboid` calls + culling exemption for neighbors.
- **Collision**: first partial-Y branch in `collidesAt` (`queries.ts`) — full 3D AABB overlap per box (doors do partial X/Z; this adds Y). Mobs share `collidesAt` → automatic.
- **Auto-step** (the load-bearing new mechanic, its own commit): in `stepAxis` (x/z, grounded only), on collision probe `+STEP_UP_HEIGHT` then back down to the landing; commit if clear, else revert. `STEP_UP_HEIGHT = 0.55` — steps 0.5 rises (slabs/stairs), does **not** step full blocks (1.0), which is Minecraft-parity. Server pose clamp tolerates it (`+0.6` vertical slack in `applyRemotePose`); noclip/flying bypass naturally; verify crouch edge-guard still holds.
- **Support rules**: slabs/stairs are NOT valid support for doors/redstone/rails — extend the shared support predicate in `mining.ts` + `redstone.ts` phase 1 (the same seams group 1's rails extended — same branch, no merge friction). Lighting: keep opaque (doors precedent; documented). `createSurfaceYAt` in `spawn.ts`: `topY + 0.5` when top block is slab/stair so mobs don't hover.
- **Recipes**: `3 material → 6 slabs`, `6 material → 4 stairs`, for planks/stone/cobble (Building category). Online prediction: stairs facing derives from the cmd yaw on both sides → same id; add one prediction test.

**Files**: `blocks.ts` (75–89 + colors), new `slabs.ts`, `meshing.ts`, `queries.ts`, `playerMotion.ts` (+`config.ts` `STEP_UP_HEIGHT`), `mining.ts` (stair placement + support predicate), `redstone.ts` (support), `spawn.ts`, `items.ts` (6 items, `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` for all 15 ids), `recipes.ts`, `audio/materials.ts` (15 rows).

**Commits**: (1) `feat(world)` blocks/shapes/meshing/partial collision; (2) `feat(engine)` auto step-up (own commit — global movement-feel change, flagged in CHANGELOG); (3) `feat(items)` items/facing placement/recipes; (4) `docs`.

**Tests**: new `slabs.test.ts` (id↔state, bounds), `queries.test.ts` (partial-Y overlap cases), new `meshing.test.ts` (slab 6 faces, stair 12, neighbor keeps face), step-up tests (up slab/stair, blocked by 1.0 wall, no mid-air step, crouch edge-guard intact), `mining.test.ts` (facing from yaw ×4), prediction test. **e2e: smoke extension** — creative-place a stair, walk into it, assert `y` rises without a jump (feel regression invisible to unit tests).

**Deferrals**: top slabs, double-slabs, more materials, inner/outer stair corners, light transmission, culled partial meshing.

---

## Docs (per feature group, shipping in that group's docs commit; AGENTS.md map)

`architecture.md` (group 1: per-kind vehicle support + coasting tick + rails-in-redstone; group 3: partial-Y collision + auto-step invariants), `adding-content.md` (group 1: "new vehicle kind" recipe + rail as redstone example; group 3: "partial-shape block" recipe), `tuning.md` (each group's config block), `manual.md`, `reference.md` (blocks/recipes/mobs tables), `testing.md` (coverage rows), `CHANGELOG.md` (one entry per feature; group 3's flags the movement change). README controls unchanged.

## Verification

`bun run lint` + `bun run format:check` locally per commit ([[local-verify-format-lint-only]]); full gate once before opening the PR: `typecheck`, `bun test` (mind exit 99 = passed-but-leaked), `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e` (renderer/movement are touched by groups 1 and 3) — **check port 3000 is free first** (known collision gotcha). Manual gameplay pass items to flag in the PR body: cart ride feel + rail visuals, drowned look/pacing on an ocean seed at night, stair step feel + shapes. One PR via `gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main` (only when the user asks to push/open it), conventional commits with why-bodies, no attribution lines. Note: main's e2e gate currently has two known pre-existing flakes (touch + multiplayer lagged-break) — unrelated to this work, wants its own session.

export const WORLD_SIZE_X = 512;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Y = 150;

export const enum BlockId {
  Air = 0,
  Grass = 1,
  Dirt = 2,
  Stone = 3,
  Wood = 4,
  Leaves = 5,
  Bedrock = 6,
  Planks = 7,

  Snow = 18,
  Cactus = 19,
  Bed = 20,
  Farmland = 21,
  // Wheat growth stages — consecutive ids so a crop advances by +1 (see randomTicks.ts).
  WheatStage0 = 22,
  WheatStage1 = 23,
  WheatStage2 = 24,
  WheatStage3 = 25,
  Furnace = 26,
  Chest = 27,
  // Dungeon blocks (worldgen-only flavor + the spawner block-entity marker).
  MossyCobblestone = 28,
  Spawner = 29,
  // Wood doors — 16 contiguous ids (4 facings × open/closed × lower/upper).
  // doors.ts derives state by offset from DoorNorthLower, so keep them in order.
  DoorNorthLower = 30,
  DoorNorthUpper = 31,
  DoorEastLower = 32,
  DoorEastUpper = 33,
  DoorSouthLower = 34,
  DoorSouthUpper = 35,
  DoorWestLower = 36,
